answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock a refundable bond before bidding, then release it only after independently audited work. New identities gain no influence until they complete jobs, so an attacker cannot instantly forge a trusted fleet: each fake agent ties up capital and must spend time earning reputation. Audits can compare supposedly independent outputs, whether labeling glacier melt or saffron grades; coordinated duplicates risk losing their bonds, making the attack costly even if identities are cheap.
